name: optimize_missing_index
description: Adds a missing index on users.email to speed up login lookups
prompts: schema.sql defines a `users` table used heavily for login lookups of the form `SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?`. With hundreds of thousands of rows, this query does a full table scan on every login attempt because there is no index on `email`. Add an appropriate index to schema.sql (via CREATE INDEX) so that looking up a user by email is fast, without changing the existing `users` table's columns, types, or any other behavior.

test_setup_files.test_index.py:
import sqlite3, time, random, string

def rand_email(i):
    return f"user{i}_{''.join(random.choices(string.ascii_lowercase, k=8))}@example.com"

conn = sqlite3.connect(':memory:')
with open('schema.sql', encoding='utf-8') as f:
    conn.executescript(f.read())

N = 1_000_000
REPS = 20
rows = [(i, rand_email(i), f'name{i}') for i in range(N)]
conn.executemany('INSERT INTO users (id, email, name) VALUES (?, ?, ?)', rows)
conn.commit()

targets = [rows[i][1] for i in range(N - REPS, N)]

t0 = time.monotonic()
for tgt in targets:
    cur = conn.execute('SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?', (tgt,))
    r = cur.fetchall()
    assert len(r) == 1, f'expected exactly one match for {tgt!r}, got {len(r)}'
t1 = time.monotonic()
elapsed = t1 - t0

plan = conn.execute('EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN SELECT * FROM users WHERE email = ?', (targets[0],)).fetchall()
plan_text = ' '.join(str(p) for p in plan).lower()
uses_index = 'using index' in plan_text or 'search' in plan_text
assert uses_index, f'query plan does not appear to use an index on email: {plan}'
assert elapsed < 0.5, f'{REPS} lookups by email took {elapsed:.3f}s - too slow, an index on email is required (query plan: {plan})'

print(f'PASS ({elapsed:.4f}s for {REPS} lookups)')
